questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India, in the context of the recently released September 2026 inflation data: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The WPI is released monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
The current base year of the WPI series is 2011-12.
Unlike the Consumer Price Index, the WPI basket also carries a weight for services such as housing and education.
Fuel and power constitutes a separate major group in the WPI basket, distinct from primary articles and manufactured products.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry) on a 2011-12 base, with Fuel & Power as a distinct major group alongside Primary Articles and Manufactured Products. Statement 3 is false — WPI measures wholesale/producer prices of goods only and excludes services, which is precisely why CPI (which includes housing, education, health) is used for inflation targeting instead.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Wholesale inflation rises to 11.39% in September on jump in fuel, food, manufactured products prices
questions.pyqLink: Tests WPI vs CPI methodology and institutional ownership; similar to UPSC 2015/2019 questions distinguishing WPI and CPI coverage and base years.

questions.stem: With reference to quantum computing, in the context of Microsoft's new 'topological' quantum chip, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: A qubit can exist in a superposition of the 0 and 1 states simultaneously, unlike a classical bit.
The Majorana fermion is a hypothetical particle that acts as its own antiparticle, and is relevant to topological quantum computing.
A topological qubit stores quantum information primarily using the spin orientation of a single trapped ion held in an electromagnetic field.
Once a company's press release describes a technological claim in detail, peer review of the underlying scientific paper becomes unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — superposition is the defining property of a qubit, and the Majorana fermion (its own antiparticle) underlies the non-abelian anyon states topological computing exploits. Statement 3 is false — storing information via a trapped ion's spin describes trapped-ion quantum computing, a different and competing approach, not the topological route. Statement 4 is false and contradicts the article's own point: the gap between Microsoft's press release and its more circumspect peer-reviewed paper is exactly why independent verification matters.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Old doubts linger, yet new Microsoft quantum chip raises the stakes
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic concepts of qubits and quantum computing approaches, an emerging area UPSC has begun probing (cf. UPSC 2023 question on quantum computing applications).

questions.stem: With reference to the GST Council, whose 57th meeting recently cleared farm-related tax concessions, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution of India.
Every decision of the GST Council must be taken by a unanimous vote of all its members, as mandated by the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the GST Council was constituted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 under Article 279A. Statement 2 is incorrect — decisions are taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes cast, with the Centre's vote weighted at one-third and all states' votes combined weighted at two-thirds; unanimity is not constitutionally required.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Mint Explainer: What do the GST Council's latest tax cuts mean for India's farmers?
questions.pyqLink: Classic Article 279A/GST Council composition and voting-weightage question, a recurring UPSC favourite (cf. UPSC 2017, 2019 on GST Council powers).

questions.stem: With reference to disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) in India, in the context of the Centre nearing its Rs 80,000 crore disinvestment target via the IDBI Bank stake sale, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) is the nodal department for disinvestment of CPSEs under the Ministry of Finance.
Strategic disinvestment, by definition, requires the government to retain at least 51% equity and management control in the CPSE after the transaction.
Disinvestment proceeds are currently credited to the Public Account of India and may be utilized, among other things, to finance the capital expenditure of the government.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: DIPAM under the Finance Ministry steers CPSE disinvestment, and proceeds flow into the Public Account (via the National Investment Fund mechanism merged into it in 2013) and can fund capital expenditure. Statement 2 is incorrect — strategic disinvestment is precisely the opposite: it involves transferring substantial government shareholding and management control to a private entity, with equity often falling well below 51%.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Centre set to cross Rs 80000 cr disinvestment target for first time since FY19 after IDBI Bank stake sale
questions.pyqLink: Tests the strategic disinvestment concept and DIPAM's institutional role, building on UPSC's recurring interest in disinvestment policy (cf. UPSC 2020 Air India/BPCL-era questions).

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of international groupings and a statement about each, in the context of the ongoing discussion on the growing role of 'middle powers' in the global order: How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Includes 19 individual countries, the European Union and the African Union as members
Originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, with South Africa joining in 2010
A formal defence treaty alliance obligating India, the US, Japan and Australia to mutual military defence
An intergovernmental forum of seven advanced economies of which India is a permanent member
questions.explanation: G20 and BRICS are correctly matched — the African Union joined G20 as a permanent member in 2023, and South Africa joined the original BRIC grouping in 2010. Quad is wrongly matched — it is an informal strategic dialogue among India, the US, Japan and Australia with no treaty obligation of mutual defence. G7 is wrongly matched — India is only occasionally invited as a guest, not a permanent member, of this forum of advanced economies.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: 'Board of directors is expanding': Jaishankar pitches bigger role for 'middle powers' in changing global order
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional nature of key groupings (G20, BRICS, Quad, G7) often conflated by candidates; similar to UPSC's recurring pairs-matched questions on regional/plurilateral groupings.

questions.stem: With reference to recent developments in quantum computing, which one of the following best describes a 'topological qubit'?
options: A qubit built using a superconducting loop cooled to near absolute zero, where information is stored in the direction of current flow
A qubit realised by trapping a single ion in an electromagnetic field and manipulating its energy levels with lasers
A qubit that uses the polarization state of a single photon to represent quantum information for secure communication
A qubit that encodes information in the non-local braiding properties of quasiparticles such as Majorana zero modes, making it intrinsically more resistant to local environmental noise
questions.explanation: A topological qubit, as pursued by Microsoft's 'topoconductor' material, stores information in the non-local topological properties of quasiparticles (Majorana zero modes), which in principle makes the stored information harder to disturb through local noise. Options (a) and (b) describe superconducting and trapped-ion qubits respectively — rival, non-topological approaches — while option (c) describes photonic qubits used mainly in quantum communication, not topological computing.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Old doubts linger, yet new Microsoft quantum chip raises the stakes
questions.pyqLink: Conceptual 'best describes the term' format applied to an emerging technology, akin to UPSC 2019's 'Merchant Discount Rate' question style.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of India's external sector challenges: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: Statement-I: India's current account deficit is structurally driven to a large extent by its import dependence on oil, gas and gold.
Statement-II: A widening current account deficit increases downward pressure on the domestic currency by raising the net demand for foreign exchange.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are independently correct — India's CAD is heavily a function of oil, gas and gold imports, as noted by BCG's Janmejaya Sinha, and a wider CAD does raise forex demand that pressures the rupee. However, Statement-II explains a consequence of a widening CAD on the currency, not the cause of why the CAD itself is structurally driven by energy and gold imports — so it is not the correct explanation for Statement-I.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Fixing current account deficit key to stablizing rupee: BCG's Janmejaya Sinha
questions.pyqLink: Statement-I/II format on balance of payments concepts, in the style introduced from UPSC 2022-23 onward on economic causation.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE), under which Kerala has launched India's first State-level assessment. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) protocol used for such assessments was developed by the IUCN.
Kerala's initiative is the first instance of any Indian State undertaking an ecosystem-level, rather than species-level, conservation assessment.
Under the RLE framework, ecosystems that have completely and irreversibly transformed are categorised as 'Extinct', the same term used in the species Red List.
Myristica swamps, cited among Kerala's threatened ecosystems, are freshwater swamp forests found in parts of the Western Ghats.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the RLE protocol is an IUCN framework, Kerala's project is indeed India's first State-level ecosystem assessment, and myristica swamps are genuine freshwater swamp forests of the Western Ghats. Statement 3 is wrong because the RLE uses the term 'Collapsed' (not 'Extinct') for ecosystems that have irreversibly transformed, deliberately distinguishing ecosystem assessment from species assessment.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Why Keralam has launched India's first ecosystem Red List assessment
questions.pyqLink: Tests IUCN Red List of Ecosystems category terminology versus the species Red List; similar in style to UPSC 2023's Ramsar Convention criteria statement question.

questions.stem: The appointment of a State Governor has again drawn public protest. Consider the following statements on the constitutional office of Governor. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President under Article 155 of the Constitution.
The Constitution requires a person to be a permanent resident of the State concerned to be eligible for appointment as its Governor.
A Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, notwithstanding the five-year term prescribed under Article 156.
Unlike the President, a Governor cannot address the State Legislature at the commencement of its first session after a general election.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct — the President appoints the Governor under Article 155. Statement 2 is wrong because the Constitution prescribes no residency requirement (only citizenship and minimum age of 35 under Article 157); by convention, Governors are usually appointed from outside the State. Statement 3 is a trick reversal — the pleasure doctrine and the five-year term coexist, not 'notwithstanding' one another, but more importantly statement 4 is simply false since Article 176 obliges the Governor to address the Legislature, just as the President addresses Parliament under Article 87.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi meet murdered Ankita Bhandari’s parents as they protest Sikkim Governor appointment
questions.pyqLink: Tests Articles 155-158 and 176 on the Governor's appointment, tenure and functions; similar to recurring UPSC questions on gubernatorial powers and conventions.

questions.stem: With reference to the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), which recorded a series-high of 11.4% in September 2026, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Wholesale Price Index is compiled by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Unlike the Consumer Price Index, the Wholesale Price Index does not capture prices of services.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: WPI covers only goods (primary articles, fuel and power, and manufactured products) and excludes services, unlike the broader CPI basket. Statement 1 is wrong because WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not by the NSO/MoSPI, which compiles the CPI.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Food and fuel push wholesale inflation to series-high of 11.4% in September 2026
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional and conceptual distinction between WPI and CPI; similar to UPSC 2022's statement-based question on Indian economy inflation indices.

questions.stem: With reference to the regulatory framework for satellite-based internet services in India, as highlighted by the Starlink-Jio entry debate, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Spectrum for satellite-based communication services in India is assigned administratively rather than through auction, as recommended by TRAI.
The Telecommunications Act, 2023 provides the legal basis for administrative assignment of spectrum for specified uses, including satellite-based services.
GMPCS (Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite) is a licence category under which satellite communication service providers operate in India.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. TRAI recommended, and the government accepted, administrative (not auction-based) allocation of satellite spectrum; the Telecommunications Act, 2023 explicitly lists such administrative assignment in its First Schedule; and GMPCS is indeed the licence category governing satellite phone and internet operators like Starlink in India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Starlink, Jio and the battle for India's satellite internet | In Focus Podcast
questions.pyqLink: Tests the auction-versus-administrative spectrum allocation debate and the Telecommunications Act, 2023; builds on UPSC's recurring spectrum-auction questions (e.g., 2G/2017-style).

questions.stem: Thailand's deliberate flooding of villages to protect Bangkok has drawn attention to the river systems of mainland Southeast Asia. Consider the following pairs of rivers and the water body each ultimately drains into. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Chao Phraya (through central Thailand), Irrawaddy (through Myanmar) and Salween (through Myanmar) are correctly matched with their respective outlets. The Mekong is wrongly paired — after flowing through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, it empties into the South China Sea via the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, not the Gulf of Thailand.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Thailand floods villages to protect capital
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical geography of Southeast Asian transboundary rivers and their outflow seas; in the style of UPSC's river-matching questions.

questions.stem: The Jeypore ground gecko was first described in 1878, presumed extinct for roughly 130 years, and then rediscovered in 2010 in Odisha. Which one of the following best describes a species of this kind in conservation biology?
options: A 'Lazarus taxon' — a species that reappears in the observational or fossil record after a long period during which it was believed extinct
A species that was never formally described in scientific literature prior to its rediscovery
A species classified as 'Extinct in the Wild' because only captive-bred populations had survived during the interim period
A species that, being confined to protected areas, is ineligible for assessment under the IUCN Red List
questions.explanation: Such species are termed 'Lazarus taxa' in conservation biology — organisms rediscovered after being presumed extinct for an extended period, exactly matching the gecko's history of an 1878 description followed by a 2010 rediscovery. It was formally described well before its rediscovery (ruling out option 2), no captive population was involved (ruling out option 3), and confinement to a habitat does not exempt a species from Red List assessment (ruling out option 4).
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Mining project threatens future of rare Jeypore ground gecko
questions.pyqLink: Tests the conservation-biology concept of 'Lazarus taxon' and rediscovered species; mirrors UPSC's 'best describes the term' format (e.g., 2019 Merchant Discount Rate question).

questions.stem: With reference to the recent appreciation of the rupee against the US dollar, consider the following two statements.
statements: Statement-I: The Reserve Bank of India intervenes in the foreign exchange market by buying or selling US dollars to curb excessive volatility in the rupee's exchange rate.
Statement-II: Under India's current exchange rate regime, the RBI is mandated to maintain the rupee at a fixed peg against the US dollar.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: the RBI routinely intervenes in spot and forward forex markets to smooth excessive volatility, as seen in the rupee's recent gains. Statement-II is incorrect because India follows a market-determined, managed-float exchange rate regime, not a fixed peg — the RBI's mandate is to curb volatility, not to defend a fixed rate against the dollar.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Rupee rises 19 paise to close at 95.17 against U.S. dollar
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between a managed float and a fixed exchange rate regime, and the RBI's forex intervention role; in the style of UPSC 2023's Statement-I/Statement-II economy questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The CBI derives its powers of investigation from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
Employees of a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) are not treated as 'public servants' under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
questions.explanation: The CBI is a statutory (not constitutional) body that functions under the DSPE Act, 1946, so Statement 1 is correct. The PC Act, 1988 defines 'public servant' broadly to include officers/employees of government companies and corporations such as Munition India Limited, so Statement 2 is false — which is exactly why the arrested executive director could be booked.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CBI arrests executive director of defence firm for graft
questions.pyqLink: Tests CBI's statutory status and PC Act's definition of 'public servant', similar to UPSC 2021 question on CBI's constitutional/statutory character.

questions.stem: With reference to Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in India's defence manufacturing sector, consider the following statements: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 100% FDI is permitted in defence manufacturing under the automatic route.
FDI beyond 74% in defence manufacturing is permitted only through the government approval route.
questions.explanation: Current policy permits FDI up to 74% under the automatic route in defence manufacturing; FDI beyond 74% (up to 100%) is allowed only via the government approval route, typically where access to modern technology is involved. Statement 1 is wrong since 100% is not automatic, Statement 2 is correct — relevant to collaborations like Aequs-Safran and Czech aerospace investment in Karnataka.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Belagavi-based Aequs announces long-term supply agreements with Safran for aerospace applications
questions.pyqLink: Tests FDI policy caps/routes by sector, a recurring UPSC theme (e.g., insurance FDI cap questions in 2021-22).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the classification of hydropower in India: How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: Hydropower projects with installed capacity above 25 MW are classified as 'Large Hydro' projects.
Large hydropower projects have been declared a renewable energy source by the Government of India.
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry for hydropower projects of all capacities.
Small hydro projects, with capacity up to 25 MW, are promoted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: projects above 25 MW are 'Large Hydro', the government in 2019 declared large hydro a renewable source, and MNRE promotes small hydro (up to 25 MW). Statement 3 is false — large hydro projects fall under the Ministry of Power/CEA, not MNRE, which handles only small hydro.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Karnataka asks Czech companies to invest beyond Bengaluru
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional and capacity-based classification of hydropower as renewable energy, triggered by Karnataka's mention of its solar and hydro plants.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about boundary lines in the Jammu and Kashmir region: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Line of Control (LoC) separates Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) and is not an internationally recognised boundary.
The Line of Actual Control (LAC) demarcates the India-Pakistan boundary in the Siachen Glacier area.
Pakistan-occupied Kashmir includes the regions of Gilgit-Baltistan and so-called 'Azad Kashmir'.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the LoC is a ceasefire line from the 1972 Simla Agreement, not a legal international border. Statement 3 is correct — PoK comprises Gilgit-Baltistan and 'Azad Kashmir'. Statement 2 is wrong: the LAC is the India-China boundary; the India-Pakistan line in Siachen is called the Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL), not the LAC.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: India asks when UN body will report on PoK human rights concerns
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between LoC, LAC and AGPL — a frequent UPSC trap on India's boundary lines, prompted by India's UN statement on PoK.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of international prizes in mathematics/computing and their administering bodies: How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
questions.explanation: Fields Medal is awarded by the International Mathematical Union, the Abel Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, and the Turing Award by the ACM — all correct. The Nobel Prize in Physics is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, not the International Mathematical Union, making the fourth pair incorrect.

questions.stem: With reference to 'Durga Puja in Kolkata', which one of the following best describes its recognition at the international level?
options: It is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as a cultural heritage site.
It is inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
It is recognised by UNESCO under the Memory of the World programme for documentary heritage.
It is designated a UNESCO Creative City for crafts and folk art.
questions.explanation: Kolkata's Durga Puja was inscribed in 2021 on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, recognising it as a living social and artistic practice. The World Heritage List covers tangible monuments/sites, the Memory of the World programme covers documentary archives, and the Creative Cities Network is a separate UNESCO designation for cities — none apply here.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: India's largest red light area in Kolkata's Sonagachi inaugurates Durga Puja
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between UNESCO's different heritage lists/programmes, a recurring static concept (e.g., UPSC questions on Intangible Cultural Heritage List entries from India).
